detail:
Mayo Clinic's fibromyalgia guidance describes treatment as a combination rather than a single therapy. Self-care carries much of the load: regular exercise, stress management, good sleep habits, and pacing activity. Psychological and behavioral therapies, including cognitive behavioral therapy, help many people change how pain is processed and coped with, and physical or occupational therapy can support function.

Medicines a clinician may prescribe include the FDA-approved fibromyalgia drugs duloxetine, milnacipran, and pregabalin, and sometimes other antidepressants or anti-seizure medicines used for pain. Mayo notes that anti-inflammatory pain relievers have limited effect on fibromyalgia pain itself, and opioids are not recommended.

Talk to your doctor before starting or changing any medication.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material.
summary: Mayo Clinic describes fibromyalgia care as a combination: regular exercise, stress and sleep strategies, psychological and behavioral therapy, and medicines for some people, while opioids are not recommended for this condition.
takeaways: exercise is a core treatment, started gently
cbt and stress management can reduce symptom impact
approved medicines include duloxetine, milnacipran, and pregabalin
never start or stop these medicines without your doctor
title: Managing fibromyalgia: a combined approach
